real_qa.q: What percentage of products and materials around us have been touched by chemistry according to Nurion?
real_qa.r: According to Vivi Holler, 96% of everything around us has been touched by chemistry. This includes devices, computers, cars and electric vehicles, personal care products, pharmaceuticals, paint, and building materials. The chemistry industry is referred to as the mother of all industries because it feeds into all other end markets, and improvements made within chemicals manufacturing trickle through the entire value chain.

real_qa.q: How does Nurion approach sustainability as a business strategy rather than ideology?
real_qa.r: Nurion sees sustainability as foundational for growth and as a genuine growth lever. It starts with answering customer demand for safer, more natural, biodegradable, or durable products, which drives top-line growth. The company also improves operational efficiency through less energy and water use, lowering costs and protecting its license to operate. Additionally, employees increasingly want to work for companies that do it right, making people investment crucial.
real_qa.requete: Nurion sustainability growth lever business case

real_qa.q: What are the main challenges Nurion faces in scaling low-carbon and bio-based chemical products?
real_qa.r: The primary challenge is that low-carbon products can come at a premium, and switching to alternative feedstock requires available feeds at scale, which is not always the case. When feedstocks are in niche supply, they command premium pricing. Consumers often cannot afford sustainable choices at higher prices due to inflation and energy costs, so the industry must work across the value chain with customers and suppliers to deliver high-performance, sustainable products at the right cost.
real_qa.requete: low-carbon chemicals scale price premium challenge

real_qa.q: Why did Nurion's CEO Charlie Shaver ask Vivi Holler to lead sustainability despite her communications background?
real_qa.r: CEO Charlie Shaver hired Vivi to lead sustainability and communications during the company's early years as a standalone entity following the 2018 spin-off from Axo Nobel. Though she lacked formal sustainability experience, Shaver recognized that her non-chemistry background was valuable for helping explain complex technical concepts to non-specialists. She then completed an eight-week Cambridge course to build her sustainability knowledge while managing the responsibilities during COVID.
real_qa.requete: Nurion Charlie Shaver sustainability communications transition

real_qa.q: What are the different customer needs Nurion addresses across its bio-based and circular chemistry portfolios?
real_qa.r: Nurion's customers have diverse needs. Home and personal care customers want natural, bio-based, and biodegradable products. However, other customers value durability over biodegradability—for example, paint should last as long as possible on a wall. Nurion also produces organic peroxides used in wind turbines and insulation for high-voltage cables, where biodegradability is undesirable. These competing demands mean the company must tailor sustainable solutions to specific customer requirements.
real_qa.requete: Nurion bio-based circular chemistry customer needs

guest.bio_context: Vivi Holler wrote her master's thesis on corporate social responsibility and worked at Heineken and communications agency Flashman Hillard before joining Axo Nobel. When the Specialty Chemicals Division was spun off and sold to the Carlyle Group in 2018, she led the carve-out communications and brand launch of the new company. Shortly after becoming standalone, CEO Charlie Shaver asked her to lead sustainability alongside communications. Though she lacked formal sustainability experience, she completed an eight-week Cambridge course during COVID and has since transitioned to focus exclusively on sustainability at Nurion.
